lead.headline: Circle secures national bank charter as US CBDC ban heads to law, reshaping the stablecoin-regulatory axis
lead.tldr: The US is simultaneously blocking a digital dollar and elevating private stablecoins to federal banking status, creating a structural policy bias toward bank-issued digital dollars that rewards incumbents and complicates any future public alternative.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, here is what moved in Web3 over the last 24 hours and why the stablecoin-regulatory axis is the signal to track for the quarter ahead.

top_signals.title: US CBDC Ban to Go into Effect without Trump Signoff on Housing Bill
top_signals.summary: A bipartisan US housing bill that includes a ban on the issuance of a digital dollar (CBDC) until 2030 is set to become law. The legislation will take effect even without President Trump's explicit signature due to a 10-day inaction period.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The CBDC ban until 2030 removes the existential competitive threat to private stablecoins and entrenches USDC, PYUSD, and bank-issued tokens as the default digital dollar infrastructure, with implications for monetary policy transmission and fintech moats.

top_signals.title: USDC issuer Circle wins final approval for US national trust bank charter20m
top_signals.summary: Circle, the issuer of the USDC stablecoin, has received final approval for a US national trust bank charter. This regulatory milestone allows the company to operate as a federally chartered bank, enhancing its legitimacy and operational capabilities within the US financial system.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Circle's national trust bank charter is the first of its kind for a crypto-native issuer and sets a regulatory template that raises compliance costs for smaller competitors while giving USDC preferential access to Fed accounts and payment rails.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin bulls Michael Saylor, Adam Back slam BIP-110 Ordinals proposal34m, Bitcoin bulls Michael Saylor, Adam Back slam BIP-110 Ordinals proposalThe ongoing debate comes despite a broad downturn in Ordinals transaction activity over the last two years.
top_signals.summary: Prominent Bitcoin figures Michael Saylor and Adam Back have expressed strong opposition to the BIP-110 proposal regarding Ordinals. The debate centers on the impact of Ordinals on the network, occurring amidst a general decline in Ordinals transaction activity.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Saylor and Back's opposition to BIP-110 reveals a persistent fault line in Bitcoin governance where store-of-value maximalists resist any protocol change that could increase chain state, even as Ordinals activity fades, suggesting future upgrade friction regardless of demand.

top_signals.title: Hedera lending protocol Bonzo Lend hit for $9 million after Supra verifier accepts manipulated price update
top_signals.summary: The Hedera-based lending protocol Bonzo Lend suffered a $9 million exploit due to a manipulated price update accepted by a Supra verifier. While most funds were drained, a white hat hacker has claimed approximately $1 million and pledged to return it.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The Bonzo Lend exploit via a manipulated Supra oracle update exposes how verifier-network centralization in supposedly decentralized oracle systems creates single-point-of-failure risks that underwriters of DeFi credit must price explicitly.

top_signals.title: Here's what's next for the Clarity Act as Congress returns to Washington
top_signals.summary: The U.S. Congress is preparing to resume sessions in Washington to address cryptocurrency legislation, specifically the Clarity Act. This legislative push is expected to occur before the midterm election schedule begins.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The Clarity Act's positioning before midterms indicates that crypto legislation has become a bipartisan campaign variable, meaning the window for structural rulemaking is narrow and likely to produce rushed, politically optimized rather than technically optimized outcomes.

deals.summary: TeraWulf is reportedly seeking a $3.5 billion debt raise to fund the development of a data center linked to AI firm Anthropic. This move signals a strategic pivot or expansion from pure Bitcoin mining into high-performance computing (HPC) and AI infrastructure.

on_the_radar.title: Binance co-CEO says 70% of EU withdrawals went to self-custody after MiCA deadline, with just 30% going to licensed platforms
on_the_radar.summary: Binance co-CEO Richard Teng reported that 70% of EU users who withdrew funds following the exchange's service suspension opted for self-custody. Only 30% of these withdrawals were directed toward other MiCA-licensed platforms.

on_the_radar.title: 'Communication challenge, nothing more': Standard Chartered keeps $100,000 bitcoin target, calls Strategy selloff a signaling problem
on_the_radar.summary: Standard Chartered maintains its price target of $100,000 for Bitcoin by the end of 2026. The bank views the recent selloff related to MicroStrategy's strategic pivot as a communication and signaling issue rather than a solvency crisis.

on_the_radar.title: Revolut integrates its crypto exchange with AI assistants as agentic trading spreads
on_the_radar.summary: Revolut has integrated its crypto exchange with several AI assistants, including Claude and Gemini. This allows users to analyze data, backtest strategies, and execute trades using agentic AI prompts.

on_the_radar.title: DOJ to drop charges against man accused in $722 million BitClub crypto Ponzi scheme: Bloomberg
on_the_radar.summary: The DOJ is reportedly considering dropping charges against an individual involved in the $722 million BitClub crypto Ponzi scheme. The move follows requests from several parties, including a former contestant on 'The Apprentice'.

on_the_radar.title: Japan’s CRYL Offers Bitcoin-Backed Loans of Up to $6.2M
on_the_radar.summary: Japanese lender CRYL has introduced Bitcoin-backed loans allowing users to borrow up to $6.2 million. This move expands the crypto-backed financing landscape within the Japanese market.

on_the_radar.title: Ledger researchers disclose Tangem card flaw; Tangem says risk to everyday users is 'virtually non-existent'
on_the_radar.summary: Ledger researchers have identified a vulnerability in Tangem cards that allows for a laser attack to reset passwords by bypassing firmware checks. Tangem has responded by stating that the risk to the average user is virtually non-existent.

on_the_radar.title: Metaplanet Studies Bitcoin-backed Digital Bonds in Japan
on_the_radar.summary: Metaplanet is exploring the development of digital corporate bonds and credit instruments within Japan. The company intends to utilize Bitcoin as collateral to enhance credit and improve efficiency in the bond market.

worth_a_read.note: Galaxy's memecoin analysis offers a useful contrarian frame on whether recent volume resurgence reflects genuine retail re-entry or just rotational liquidity within a shrinking active-user base, which matters for timing any exposure to consumer-facing infra.

linkedin_post: A lot of people saw the CBDC ban and the Circle charter as separate stories. That is the wrong read. Congress is blocking a digital dollar until 2030, and the same week Circle wins a national trust bank charter as a federally regulated issuer. The policy logic is coherent: the US is outsourcing digital dollar infrastructure to private banks rather than building public rails. Circle now sits at the center of that. For investors, the market is pricing this as a regulatory win for stablecoins broadly, but the value proposition is shifting from protocol-level decentralization to bank-level compliance and balance-sheet scale. The charter raises the barrier to compete with USDC; it does not democratize it. I'd watch how Tether responds on US licensing, and whether any challenger can underwrite the compliance cost to compete. The repricing to watch is not stablecoin market cap, it is stablecoin issuer equity and debt, and how those trade versus regional bank multiples once the Fed window opens. I bet that changes.
